title: Cebiche, Chifa and Nikkei: Passive Se or Impersonal Se?

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know passive *se* and impersonal *se* from B1 Unit 6, and the personal *a* from A1 Unit 24, and you know that you must tell them apart (B2 Unit 19): *se* + a noun, and the verb agrees with it (*Se sirven los cebiches fríos*); *se* with no noun, and the verb stays singular (*En Lima se come muy bien*); *se* + a particular person with *a*, and the verb stays singular too (*Se invitó a los vecinos*). Food writing uses all three.

sections.title: At work on the topic
rows: Se prepara el cebiche con pescado crudo y limón.
En Lima se come muy bien.
no noun: the verb stays singular
Se invitó a los vecinos a probar el cebiche.
particular people with *a*: the verb stays singular

items.spanish: Se prepara el cebiche con pescado crudo y limón.
items.english: Cebiche is prepared with raw fish and lime.

items.spanish: En Lima se come muy bien.
items.english: In Lima people eat very well.

items.spanish: Se invitó a los vecinos a probar el cebiche.
items.english: The neighbours were invited to try the cebiche.

sections.content: Ask what follows the verb. A thing: the verb agrees (*se sirven los cebiches*). A particular person: *a* and a singular verb (*se invitó a los vecinos*). Nothing: singular (*se come bien*). Do not write *se invitaron a los vecinos*.
